# Autocomplete skills

Add predictive text and inline gray suggestions to the **human user's chat input**
with [Autocomplete by HyperWrite](https://autocomplete.dev/add-autocomplete).
The `add-autocomplete` skill guides a coding agent through integrating the hosted
service into an existing app while preserving its login, editor and send flow.
Tab accepts one word at a time.

## Install the skill

Requires Node.js 22.20.0+ for the `skills` installer (current `skills@1.9.0`).

```sh
npx skills add OthersideAI/autocomplete-skills --skill add-autocomplete
```

This installs agent instructions from this repository. It does not install the
SDK, connect an account, configure deployment secrets, or complete the app's
integration. Ask your coding agent to use `add-autocomplete` in your app.

The skill then uses `npx @hyperwrite/autocomplete-cli init --json` for local SDK
and configuration setup. If a connection is needed, the CLI's `connect` command
requires the account owner's browser approval and accurate app details; existing
private backend credentials can also be reused. Keep the server key on the
backend, never in chat or frontend code. The agent must adapt and test the app's
own authentication and composer. Installation alone is not a working feature.

## When to use it

- Add predictive text, inline suggestions or Tab-to-complete to a human chat input.
- Integrate an existing React textarea, Next.js chat composer with a server route,
  or native HTML textarea with the hosted Autocomplete service.

This completes the person's draft; it does not generate assistant replies, replace
the app's login, or provide a self-hosted model. Rich-text/contenteditable editors
need separate integration work. Desktop English is the qualified starting point;
mobile keyboards and other languages need explicit testing. App setup requires
Node.js 22+, Git and macOS, Linux or WSL; native Windows private-key storage is not
supported by the CLI in this release. Service access and resource limits apply.
